title: ScalingPolicy
description: The job objective / reward model (ENT-34, ADR-29; part of the native distributed accelerated compute pass for UC-1 churn — ARC-11 / #264). A per-job reward objective an autoscaler optimizes — minimize cost, hit a runtime/latency target, or size the fleet to the data shape — inside hard bounds (a min/max node envelope and a cost cap). A pure value type carried on a ComputeJob by id (scaling_policy in compute_job.schema.json). Mirrored by zetta::ScalingPolicy in include/zetta/scaling_policy.hpp and enforced by ScalingPolicy::from_json() in src/core/scaling_policy.cpp — keep them in sync. A malformed policy is rejected at the boundary so the autoscaler never silently widens what it will do.

objective.description: What the autoscaler optimizes. Append-only enum (the lowercase name is the stored identifier).

bounds.description: The hard envelope the autoscaler stays inside, whatever the objective wants.

target_seconds.description: The runtime/latency target in seconds for the 'runtime_target' objective — the wall-clock the autoscaler sizes the fleet to hit. Required (> 0) when objective is 'runtime_target'; omitted/0 (unset) otherwise.

bounds.description: The min/max node envelope and the cost cap. A job needs at least one node, so min_nodes >= 1 and max_nodes >= min_nodes. cost_cap is a spend ceiling in abstract cost units (e.g. node-seconds or dollars); 0 (or omitted) means unlimited.

max_nodes.description: Ceiling on the node count (>= min_nodes).

cost_cap.description: Spend ceiling in abstract cost units. 0 (or omitted) means unlimited. Breaching it sheds the fleet back to min_nodes regardless of objective.
